Customer name/mobile line redacted (black bar) before committing. The date extraction was originally masked by a harness-adjacent production bug: extractDate()'s worded-date alternative used to false-positive-match garbled OCR text ("41\nFLOR 4241") before the real numeric date could be found. FIXED (OCR-003-T08, 2026-09-25 later run): with that false-positive eliminated, the real numeric date now matches ("26/08/26" -> 2026-08-26) and this entry PASSES.
Has both 'Food Total' and 'Total' lines with different values -- real ambiguity case; the last-match selection rule still lands on the correct 525.

Sub Total and Grand Total both present with different values -- grand-total priority should still select 1947 correctly. Failure is merchant name OCR noise ("SSR Lo") and NO_DATE_FOUND -- the date was not recognisable at all on this photo (64% confidence), not a regex/pipeline defect. Unaffected by the OCR-003-T08 regex fixes (still fails on genuine noise, as expected).

KNOWN LIMITATION CANDIDATE: 'Grand Total (Rounded)  202.00' has a parenthetical between the label and the value; extractAmount's [^\d]* skip could plausibly stop early if OCR linearizes text unexpectedly. A mismatch here is a real finding, not a bad ground truth.

KNOWN LIMITATION CANDIDATE, CONFIRMED (real eval:ocr run, 2026-09-25): amountMatch fails as predicted, though the extracted value (3) doesn't match either the parenthetical-PAISA hypothesis or the true total -- this receipt has the lowest confidence in the failing set (44%), so general OCR noise on the amount line is compounding whatever the regex captures. dateMatch now passes cleanly (28-04-09 -> 2009-04-28) after the scoring-harness date fix, isolating the amount issue. UNCHANGED by OCR-003-T08's amount-label widening (still extracts 3, confirming this was never a missing-label problem for this specific receipt -- it is OCR noise on the amount line itself, out of scope for a regex fix).
Marked 'Duplicate' at the top of the receipt; Name field is an unfilled placeholder (M: 0000000000), not real customer data.

KNOWN LIMITATION, CONFIRMED (real eval:ocr run, 2026-09-25): amountMatch fails as predicted -- extractAmount's original regex had no support for a "Gross Amount" label. OCR-003-T08 (2026-09-25 later run) widened the label set to recognise "Gross Amount"/"Bill Amt", which fixed the equivalent khodiyar-dhaba case, but this entry is STILL FAILING afterward (extracted value unchanged at 1) -- meaning the true root cause here is not the missing label but OCR noise/garbling on the amount line itself (the '1' is not a plausible misread of either 699 or 640). Needs raw OCR text to diagnose further; out of scope for a regex-only fix. dateMatch passes (12/05/25 -> 2025-05-12).

KNOWN LIMITATION -- FIXED (OCR-003-T08, real eval:ocr run 2026-09-25 later): extractAmount() now recognises "Bill Amt" as a total label (previously only "Total"/"Grand Total" were recognised, and the only such line on this receipt was the pre-GST "TOTAL 216.00"). With the label widened, the correct post-GST amount (227) is now extracted and this entry PASSES -- AMBIGUOUS_AMOUNT is correctly flagged since the pre-GST Total line still also matches, which is real ambiguity worth surfacing, not a bug. Customer name line redacted (black bar) before committing.

KNOWN LIMITATION, PARTIALLY FIXED (OCR-003-T08, real eval:ocr run 2026-09-25 later): the newly-discovered worded-date false-positive bug (garbled OCR text matching as a fake date) is now fixed -- this entry's date output changed from garbage ("31\nPHO 1503") to a correct null (NO_DATE_FOUND), which is the right behavior even though it doesn't make the entry pass. The date is printed as "12-Sep-2026" (abbreviated month name with hyphens), a format extractDate still does not support -- that specific gap remains open, tracked separately, not fixed by T08. Customer name, mobile, part of the bill number and part of the merchant address were already redacted with a physical yellow highlighter by the maintainer before this photo was taken/shared -- left as-is, not re-redacted digitally. FIXED (OCR-003-T08, real eval:ocr run 2026-09-25 later): extractDate() previously matched a misleading substring ("23-08-17") of the printed ISO date "2023-08-17" because it had no yyyy-mm-dd support and no start-of-token anchor. A dedicated ISO-date alternative, tried first, now captures the full date correctly and this entry PASSES.

Indonesian Rupiah receipt -- comma is a thousands separator here ('107,000'), which happens to parse correctly through parseAmountInput's comma-stripping. 'Total Bill' (107,107, pre-rounding) and 'Grand Total' (107,000) both present; grand-total priority should select the right one. Guest name field says 'Umum' (Indonesian for 'general/public'), not a real name. CONFIRMED (real eval:ocr run, 2026-09-25): grand-total priority worked as intended, but Tesseract dropped a zero reading the printed amount, returning 10700 instead of 107000 -- genuine OCR digit-recognition noise on this photo (76% confidence), not a pipeline bug. Unaffected by OCR-003-T08 (as expected -- this was never a regex-coverage issue).
